# Genesis AI — Mission 30 Retro Actions
**Date:** July 2026  
**Source:** Mission 30 Retro — Agents Feedback Tab (23 items)  
**Context:** All feedback was generated by teams using raw Copilot prompts in VS/GitHub Chat — NOT Genesis AI. The majority of items are closed by migration to Genesis AI. The actions below are genuine engineering gaps or planned improvements.

---

## Critical Context

The feedback is not a gap analysis of Genesis AI. It is the evidence base for the Genesis AI value proposition. Teams on raw Copilot prompts have no pipeline structure, no artefact persistence, no template contracts, no session continuity, no DCB0129 workflow, no traceability. Genesis AI closes all of these structurally on day one of migration.

The immediate priority is getting teams off raw Copilot prompts and onto Genesis AI in production.

---

## Engineering Actions (Build)

### Action 1 — Help Chat Panel in the Requirements App
**Row:** 1, 17, 20  
**What:** A persistent help chat panel in `genesis-ai-requirements-app`. Not a generic chatbot — a project-aware assistant.

**Design:**
- New conversation type in the tool — same `Conversation` pattern, same Bedrock infrastructure via existing API
- System prompt built from Genesis AI pipeline documentation — project instructions, stage descriptions, terminology, how-to guidance. Static, curated, no KG dependency
- `get_artefact` available as a tool — retrieves any approved artefact from the current project in S3 on demand. A user mid-session on P03 can ask "what did we decide in P01?" and get an answer grounded in the actual approved REQ file
- RBAC scopes artefact access — users only see artefacts from projects they have access to
- Persistent panel accessible from any pipeline stage — not a separate page. A user in a P06 session can ask a help question without navigating away

**Note:** This is not "Anthropic API" — all inference through AWS Bedrock via PrivateLink. Same infrastructure as every other pipeline stage.

**Dependency:** None — build alongside Plan 4b.

### Action 3 — SESSION-CLOSE Button (All Pipeline Stages)
**Row:** 5  
**What:** A "Close Session" button on every pipeline stage in the tool.

**Design:**
- One `SESSION-CLOSE-P0n.md` artefact per pipeline stage — not one per session, not one shared document across all stages
- Button click triggers artefact generation: stage-specific summary of what was captured, what's open, parking lot status, and a one-line "next session starts here" entry point
- Upsert behaviour — if `SESSION-CLOSE-P01.md` already exists for this project, it is updated not duplicated. Multiple sessions on the same stage produce one current file
- On session continuation via `ContinuedFromConversationId`, the `SESSION-CLOSE-P0n.md` is injected at the top of context before the first turn
- Committed to `.genesis/session-close/` in the feature repo by `genesis-ai[bot]` on generation
- Shared skill — one parameterisable skill injected at stage level, not duplicated across eight pipeline prompts. Stage-aware section headings vary per stage

**Naming convention:**
```
SESSION-CLOSE-P01.md — Requirements Discovery
SESSION-CLOSE-P02.md — Prototype Demo Builder
SESSION-CLOSE-P03.md — Architecture
SESSION-CLOSE-P04.md — Design (API/DB)
SESSION-CLOSE-P05.md — PxD
SESSION-CLOSE-P06.md — Clinical Safety
SESSION-CLOSE-P07.md — Information Governance
SESSION-CLOSE-P08.md — Security
```

**Dependency:** None — build alongside Plan 4b.

### Action 4 — Figma Option A Integration (Plan 4 Extension)
**Row:** 3, 4  
**What:** Extend the Plan 4 style reference input to accept a Figma frame URL as an alternative to PNG upload.

**Design:**
- The slot already exists: "Style reference: optional PNG uploaded by the user, fed as vision input"
- New `IFigmaImageService` — accepts a Figma frame URL, parses file key and node ID, calls Figma REST API `/v1/images/{file_key}`, returns PNG as byte array
- URL parsing: Figma URLs follow `https://www.figma.com/file/{file_key}/{title}?node-id={node_id}` — deterministic, no guessing
- PNG fed into the existing vision input path identically to a manual upload — the generation prompt does not change, the model sees a PNG either way
- Figma PAT stored as a project-level secret — not hardcoded, not per-user
- No structural change to Plan 4 generation architecture

**This is not "Figma Make"** — it is using a validated design from Figma as a style reference input to ground the EMIS-X prototype generation. The EMIS-X UI kit remains the compositional standard.

**Dependency:** Plan 4 production flag flipped. Build as Wave H.

### Action 5 — Artefact Push to Feature Repo (Plan 4b Core Deliverable)
**Row:** 12, 20  
**What:** On approval of any pipeline stage artefact, `genesis-ai[bot]` commits it to `.genesis/` in the configured feature repo (the EMIS-X product repo — Documents Manager, Consultations, Prescribing, etc.).

**Design:**
- Trigger: existing approval action in each pipeline stage — no new UI
- `GitHubIntegrationService.PushArtefactAsync` fires post-approval, routes to the correct `.genesis/` subfolder based on stage type
- Commits via the bot token already stored on the project

**Folder structure in the feature repo:**
```
.genesis/
  requirements/       — REQ-{id}.md, CHANGE-{id}.md
  architecture/       — ARCH-{id}.md
  clinical-safety/    — DCB0129-{id}.md, DCB0129-{id}.xlsx
  ig/                 — IG-{id}.md
  security/           — SEC-{id}.md
  prototype/          — index.html
  session-close/      — SESSION-CLOSE-P01.md … SESSION-CLOSE-P08.md
  project/            — PROJECT.md
```

**Artefact types pushed (all, not just markdown):**
- REQ files, CHANGE records
- Architecture documents
- DCB0129 hazard logs (MD + XLSX)
- IG/DPIA documents
- Security review documents
- Prototype HTML (`index.html`)
- SESSION-CLOSE files
- PROJECT.md (from project setup form)

**Commit convention:**
```
chore: approve REQ-001 — Unified Inbound Document Inbox
Approved-by: [user display name] ([user ERN])
Pipeline-stage: P01
Project: documents-manager-increment-1
```

**Why this matters:** The `.genesis/` folder in the feature repo becomes the living knowledge base for that product. Every requirement, hazard, architecture decision, and prototype committed here is indexed nightly by the Knowledge Graph Service (Graph 1 — Requirements Graph). The approval action is the data feed. No manual sync. No stale context.

**Dependency:** `genesis-ai[bot]` machine user created. Plan 4b infrastructure.

### Action 6 — Project Setup Form Extension (P00 — Project Initialisation)
**Row:** 9, 16, 18  
**What:** Extend the existing project creation/edit form to capture P00 (project initialisation) fields. These are captured once, stored in the DB, and flow into every pipeline stage automatically. No stage needs to re-elicit this information.

**Fields to add to the form:**
- Release type (EMIS Web / EMIS-X)
- Assurance required (yes/no)
- Pilot/deployment process
- Stakeholders and roles
- Clinical Safety Officer — feeds P06, closes "named person" inconsistency (row 18)
- IG owner — feeds P07
- Security reviewer — feeds P08
- Medical Device classification flag — feeds the new MD pipeline stage when designed

**Implementation:**
- DB migration adding columns to `projects` table
- Form extension — existing `PATCH /api/v1/projects/{id}` endpoint
- On save, `genesis-ai[bot]` commits `PROJECT.md` to `.genesis/project/` in the feature repo
- Every pipeline stage reads P00 fields from project context — no re-elicitation

**RBAC note:** Because users are authenticated via RBAC, every approval, every message, every form submission is attributed to a known user with their ERN and role. The CSO field in P00 + RBAC login = complete audit trail of who confirmed what clinical safety decision and when. No separate audit system needed.

**Dependency:** Plan 4b. Small DB migration + form extension.

### Action 7 — P06 Excel Export Artefact
**Row:** 14  
**What:** On P06 approval, generate a `DCB0129-{id}.xlsx` structured hazard export alongside the `DCB0129-{id}.md` document.

**Design:**
- Generated from the approved P06 artefact content at approval time — no additional LLM call
- Schema matches the CSO's existing Excel format — one file per clinical safety area, CSO-owned
- Generated using ClosedXML (viable .NET dependency, no new infrastructure)
- Stored in S3 alongside the MD artefact
- Committed to `.genesis/clinical-safety/` by `genesis-ai[bot]` on approval
- Downloadable from the tool by any authorised user

**Dependency:** Plan 4b (artefact push infrastructure).

**Row:** 14

### Action 9 — CODEOWNERS File + Prompt Governance Convention
**Row:** 10, 19, 23  
**What:** Formalise who owns each pipeline prompt and who must approve changes to it.

**Design:**
- `CODEOWNERS` file in `genesis-ai-requirements-api` repo mapping each pipeline prompt file to its domain owner:
  ```
  src/Genesis.AI.Infrastructure/Prompts/Pipeline06*  @indra-joshi
  src/Genesis.AI.Infrastructure/Prompts/Pipeline07*  @[ig-owner]
  src/Genesis.AI.Infrastructure/Prompts/Pipeline08*  @[security-reviewer]
  ```
- GitHub PR process is the change control mechanism — version control, review gate, revert, audit trail all come for free
- Domain owners can propose prompt improvements via PR — substantial changes go through the Genesis AI requirements pipeline first; targeted fixes go direct as a PR
- `git revert` is the rollback if a prompt change degrades output quality
- The 774 unit + 120 integration test suite runs on every PR — guardrail regressions surface as test failures before merge
- RBAC in the tool + GitHub CODEOWNERS = two-layer governance. No separate platform needed

**Dependency:** None — one file, one convention document.

---

### Action 10 — Pipeline Chat Cross-Stage Artefact Access
**Row:** 20  
**What:** Every pipeline stage conversation should have `get_artefact` access to all approved artefacts in the project — not just its own stage's artefacts.

**Design:**
- `get_artefact` tool already exists and is already wired into `ConversationStreamController`
- Prompt-level instruction added to every pipeline stage: "You have access to all approved artefacts in this project via `get_artefact`. Use them to answer questions about decisions made in other pipeline stages before asking the user to repeat context."
- When a user in P06 asks "what did we decide about patient matching in P01?" — the agent retrieves `REQ-001.md` from S3 and answers from the actual approved content
- When a user in P03 asks "what hazards were identified?" — the agent pulls the P06 DCB0129 artefact
- No new tooling. No new infrastructure. Prompt change per stage, gated through CODEOWNERS

**Dependency:** CODEOWNERS in place (Action 9). Prompt change per stage.

### Planned 2 — Medical Device Pipeline (P09)
**Row:** 13  
**What:** A new pipeline stage for Medical Device regulatory compliance (UK MDR 2002 / MHRA).

**Context:**
- Requires Indra's sign-off on which EMIS-X features qualify for MDR classification before any design begins
- If in scope, P09 sits alongside P06 Clinical Safety — not after P08 Security. The regulatory logic runs in parallel with CS and IG
- The pipeline stage needs the same treatment as every other: proper requirements elicitation, a defined template contract, a specified output artefact, Indra's sign-off
- With this addition the pipeline becomes 11 stages (P01–P08 + P09 Medical Device + P10 Pre-Swarm Decision Gate + P11 TDD/Code Generation)

**Action:** Design session with Indra. No engineering work until classification scope is confirmed.
